Package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery

Class SearchOperator

java.lang.Object
org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery.SearchOperator
public final class SearchOperator extends Object
The immutable definition of a single $-search operator — its $-name, arity, the value types it applies to, and its popup help text.

A custom operator always carries its own help text; the help text of a built-in (SearchOperatorSet.standard()) operator is owned by the browser runtime, so help() is null for built-ins. A custom operator additionally may carry a SearchPredicate the in-memory context calls when it hits that $-name — Juneau never invents one. Anything else a downstream module (for example a SQL renderer) needs to attach lives in the typed extension slot: it is keyed by the extension's own Class, so this module (commons) never needs to depend on that module's types (design §5.3).

Instances are built with SearchOperator.Builder: create(String, String) starts a new custom operator, and copy() starts a modified copy of an existing one (built-in or custom).

Combinators vs. leaves

$and/$or/$not are combinators: their children are sub-expressions, not literal value arguments, and they apply to every type. Every other operator is a leaf whose arguments are literal values and whose applicability is a fixed type set (an empty type set means "applies to all types").

Example (custom operator, with a typed extension):

SearchOperator op = SearchOperator.create("$near", "Fuzzy match. Example: $near(jhon)") .types(SearchType.TEXT) .predicate((cell, args) -> fuzzy(cell, args.get(0))) .extension(MySqlRenderer.class, myRenderer) .build(); // A later consumer that knows about MySqlRenderer retrieves it back, type-safe, with no cast. Optional<MySqlRenderer> renderer = op.extension(MySqlRenderer.class);

Since:
10.0.0

  • Method Details

    • create

      public static SearchOperator.Builder create(String name, String helpText)
      Starts a new custom (application-defined) leaf operator.

      Defaults: arity 1..* (one or more arguments), applies to all value types (an empty type set), no predicate, no extensions. Narrow it with SearchOperator.Builder.minArgs(int)/SearchOperator.Builder.maxArgs(int)/ SearchOperator.Builder.types(SearchType...) and attach an evaluator with SearchOperator.Builder.predicate(SearchPredicate) (in-memory) and/or a typed SearchOperator.Builder.extension(Class, Object) (for example, a SQL renderer).

      Parameters:
      name - The operator name, including the leading $ (e.g. "$near"). Must not be null or blank and must start with $.
      helpText - The popup help text: what the operator accepts and a short example. Must not be null or blank.
      Returns:
      A new SearchOperator.Builder pre-filled with name/helpText and the defaults above.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If name is not a valid $-name or helpText is blank.

    • copy

      public SearchOperator.Builder copy()
      Starts a SearchOperator.Builder pre-filled with this operator's current state, for building a modified copy.

      The returned builder is fully independent of this instance: mutating it (or the SearchOperator it eventually builds) never affects this instance.

      Renaming is only legal for a copy of a custom operator. Both evaluation engines dispatch a built-in purely by its name() — the in-memory engine's leaf switch and SqlDialect#builtinRenderer(String) alike — so changing the name on a copy of a custom operator (one with its own predicate/ extension) is fine and gives it a fresh identity, but doing the same to a copy of a built-in operator throws IllegalArgumentException from build(). A built-in's copy may still have its help text changed freely; only its name is fixed.

      Returns:
      A new builder seeded from this operator.

    • help

      public String help()
      The human-readable help text for this operator, shown in the column-search popup.

      Built-in operators return null: their help text is owned by juneau-search.js, which the popup falls back to. Custom operators always return non-blank text, because SearchOperator.Builder.build() rejects a custom operator without it.

      Example:

      SearchOperator near = SearchOperator.create("$near", "Within N units. Example: $near(5)").build(); near.help(); // "Within N units. Example: $near(5)" SearchOperatorSet.standard().get("$eq").help(); // null

      Returns:
      The help text, or null for a built-in operator.

    • extension

      public <X> Optional<X> extension(Class<X> type)
      Looks up a typed extension previously attached with SearchOperator.Builder.extension(Class, Object).

      This is how a downstream module (for example juneau-beanquery-sql's SQL renderer) attaches its own metadata to a custom operator without this module (commons) ever depending on that module's types: the extension is keyed by its own Class, so retrieval is type-safe with no cast (design §5.3).

      Type Parameters:
      X - The extension type.
      Parameters:
      type - The extension's class, used as the lookup key. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      The extension, or Optional.empty() if none was attached under that type.
